The base template: menus, death and fallbacks

New games are seeded with editable boilerplate before the first room. Use it as a recommended starting point when it fits, or extend or replace any part to serve the brief. These are ordinary game resources, with no protected ownership or reserved template ranges.

- Logic 0 builds the menu bar once on boot (File: Save, Restore, Restart, Quit; Speed; Sound; Help), binds the classic keys (ESC opens the menu, F5/F7/F9 save, restore and restart, F1 shows help, TAB lists the inventory), turns the status line on, then runs call.v(v0) so your room logic runs first every cycle. After the room returns, logic 0 answers the menu controllers and, once per submitted line, prints the parser fallback: "I don't know the word" when the line carried an unknown word, "I don't understand that" when no said() matched. A room that answers a line without a said() match should set(f4) after its own reply so the template does not add the generic one.
- Death is a shared handler: print your death line, then call(255). It stops input and movement, plays the death sound and offers the Restore, Restart or Quit box — SPACE steps the choice, ENTER confirms, 1-3 choose directly, F7/F9/Alt-Z answer directly. A cancelled or failed restore returns to the box; the player stays dead rather than walking in a broken control mode. If you replace this handler, design and playtest the recovery or continuation behavior your game needs.
- Read logic 0 and logic 255 for their current state, controller and string usage before editing; their sources are available through read_logic. Update affected references together when reusing IDs or changing conventions. Automatic allocation avoids IDs used by the current code; explicit bindings and edits can coordinate a rewrite. Playtest boot, input and any menu/death behavior affected by your changes. A fair death still needs a fair cause: the hazard belongs in your room's picture and priority plane.

rooms.title: Millhaven Precinct
rooms.description: Dana receives Prakash's assignment at the front desk, reads the case board, and leaves for the records office or pharmacy street.

rooms.title: Records Office
rooms.description: Dana checks the delivery ledger against the driver's account and finds the warehouse route was altered.

rooms.title: Millhaven Street
rooms.description: Dana speaks with Bud and dispatch, then follows the delivery route to the pharmacy or Pier Road.

rooms.title: Millhaven Pharmacy
rooms.description: Dana documents the forced rear entry, collects a marked bottle, and gets the pharmacist's account.

rooms.title: Pier Road Warehouse
rooms.description: With the ledger and witness account connected, Dana radios backup, confronts the suspect with Bud, and returns with a defensible case.

facts.name: case_assignment
facts.text: Sergeant Prakash assigns Dana the Millhaven pharmacy break-in: test the delivery driver's account, document the scene, connect the records and witness, and file the case.

facts.name: driver_discrepancy
facts.text: The driver says he delivered two sealed antiseptic cartons to the front counter. Dispatch logged one returnable solvent drum routed to the rear warehouse door.

facts.name: pharmacy_evidence
facts.text: A bottle bearing the warehouse's blue inventory mark was left at the forced rear entry; the pharmacist heard a delivery van after closing.

facts.name: warehouse_connection
facts.text: The altered delivery ledger and pharmacist's van account tie the break-in to the Pier Road warehouse.

facts.name: backup_and_arrest
facts.text: Dana radios dispatch and takes Bud before entering; supported by the records and pharmacy evidence, she arrests the suspect.

facts.name: filed_case
facts.text: Prakash accepts the complete report after evidence, witness account, discrepancy, and arrest are documented.

quests.name: Millhaven Pharmacy Break-in
quests.description: Verify the driver's story, document the pharmacy scene, connect the delivery records and witness account to Pier Road, make a supported arrest with backup, and file the case with Prakash.

Every step of every object is judged against the control priorities under its baseline, the cel-wide row of pixels at its feet. The interpreters scan that row left to right:

- Control 0 blocks. Control 1 blocks unless ignore.blocks. Control 2 is a trigger: f3 is set for ego when ANY baseline pixel touches control 2, so a one-pixel-wide trigger line is enough and ego cannot stand across it without triggering. Control 3 is water: f0 is set only when EVERY baseline pixel is on water, so a shoreline reads as land until the whole footprint is in. obj.on.water and obj.on.land gate movement with that all-cells rule.
- Priority 15 objects skip the scan entirely and clear both flags. Fixed priority does not skip it.
- Paint barriers along the visible obstacle they represent and leave exits open; a stray control-0 pixel in a doorway is the most common walking bug. A priority fill floods the connected region, so close every outline before filling. Keep open floor at 4.
- Room edges: ego touching an edge sets v2 (1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom, 4 left) for one cycle; the room logic reads it and calls new.room. set.horizon(y) keeps ego below the sky line unless ignore.horizon.
- Scripted movement: move.obj(o, x, y, step, f) walks an object to a point and sets f on arrival. On ego it takes control away from the player until arrival or a border stop, then hands it back and zeroes v6. A zero-distance move.obj on ego is the idiom for handing control back after a scripted placement. program.control and player.control switch it explicitly; wander(o) and follow.ego(o, distance, f) are the other motions.
- reposition(o, dx, dy) moves an object by variable deltas and runs the placement check at once, so a script can slide ego along a trigger line and wait for the exact pixel where a flag fires. The Gold Rush demonstration does exactly that to reach one coordinate.
- Death and failure: when the player walks into danger, decide it from the control screen or a posn() box, print a short message with a wry line, and offer restore. Keep the dangerous area visibly different so the death is fair.
